correctness.rationale: In a strict chain, two-variable re-entrant predecessor/successor quantifiers define a given element rank/co-rank and thus its component length. Up to k pairwise incomparable such elements witness at least j chains of specified exact length; quantifier shadowing in separately evaluated length predicates does not increase variable width. In the converse permanent k-pebble game match occupied components by their exact lengths and ranks; moving a pebble leaves <=k-1 occupied components, guaranteeing an unused matching component when both multiplicities >=k. Capped multiplicities imply a unique minimum representative. Multiplicity choices 0..k at each length give product_l(1+z^l+...+z^{kl})=prod_{(k+1) not divides r}(1-z^r)^-1. Independent partition-count identities tested k=2..6 through n=17.

originality.rationale: A complete all-width strict-chain-disjoint-sum theory classification was not found in the actual compared published texts. Earlier quantifier-rank-three classification of at most three chains concerns bounded depth and contains nontrivial mergers not equivalent to unrestricted k-variable logic. Weak-order theorems classify ordinal sums of antichains and cannot be transported to incomparable disjoint chains by a mere relabeling. The Euler product identity is classical, but its exact logical-spectrum interpretation is a distinct application.

value.rationale: Disjoint unions of linear orders form a natural rich poset family. The theorem determines all unrestricted-depth counting-free k-variable theories, sharp component multiplicity cutoffs, unique minimum representatives and exact partition-theoretic theory spectrum. The connection between logical width and restricted partitions gives a useful complete classification beyond trivial single-chain examples.

final_claim: For nonempty finite posets that are disjoint unions of finite strict chains, counting-free FO^k equivalence for all k>=2 is exactly chain-length multiplicities truncated to k; minimum-size theory spectrum equals partitions with no part divisible by k+1.
